why: Two rules the BrowserAdapter has to reimplement in order to behave like the host: how a conversation gets named from what was said in it, and how a search box's raw text becomes an FTS5 expression. Both are pure functions of a string, so a table of (input) -> (expected) pins them exactly. The Rust host is the specification; these expectations were produced by it.

titleDerivation.name: plain-sentence
titleDerivation.why: the ordinary case: short enough to use verbatim
titleDerivation.input: Why is the night sky dark?
titleDerivation.expect: Why is the night sky dark?

titleDerivation.name: heading-lead-in
titleDerivation.why: a markdown heading is about its subject, not about its hashes
titleDerivation.input:
## Why the sails matter

body text follows

titleDerivation.name: quote-lead-in
titleDerivation.why: a block quote's caret is punctuation, not content

titleDerivation.name: bullet-lead-in
titleDerivation.why: a list opener is a marker; the first item is the subject

titleDerivation.name: ordered-lead-in
titleDerivation.why: `1. ` is a marker; `1` on its own would not be

titleDerivation.name: negative-number-is-not-a-bullet
titleDerivation.why: a lead-in needs the separating space, or -5 becomes 5 and the title lies

titleDerivation.name: emphasis-is-not-a-bullet
titleDerivation.why: same rule from the other side: `*emphasis*` must keep its first character

titleDerivation.name: horizontal-rule-is-skipped
titleDerivation.why: a rule strips to nothing, which correctly disqualifies the line

titleDerivation.name: code-fence-is-skipped
titleDerivation.why: a fence names a language, not a subject

titleDerivation.name: leading-blank-lines-are-skipped
titleDerivation.why: the first NON-BLANK line is the candidate

titleDerivation.name: internal-whitespace-collapses
titleDerivation.why: tabs and runs of spaces must not survive into a single-line list row

titleDerivation.name: empty-input-derives-nothing
titleDerivation.why: null means `leave the placeholder alone`, never `store an empty title`

titleDerivation.name: whitespace-only-derives-nothing
titleDerivation.why: same, for a turn that carried no text at all

titleDerivation.name: truncates-at-a-word-boundary
titleDerivation.why: a cut mid-word reads as a bug; a cut at a space reads as a summary
titleDerivation.input: The complete and unabridged history of celestial navigation in the southern hemisphere
titleDerivation.expect: The complete and unabridged history of…

titleDerivation.name: truncates-mid-word-when-there-is-no-boundary
titleDerivation.why: one long word must still yield a title rather than an empty string

titleDerivation.name: strips-trailing-punctuation-before-the-ellipsis
titleDerivation.input: Explain, in detail, the following points, and then, finally, summarise
titleDerivation.expect: Explain, in detail, the following points, and…

titleDerivation.name: counts-accented-characters-as-one-each
titleDerivation.why: Rust counts chars and JS must count code points, not UTF-16 units
titleDerivation.input: Comment analyser les données météorologiques françaises et européennes

titleDerivation.name: counts-an-emoji-by-code-point
titleDerivation.why: the variation selector is its own code point on both sides, so the cut lands identically
titleDerivation.input: 🛰️ satellite telemetry, then a very long tail that keeps going past the limit
titleDerivation.expect: 🛰️ satellite telemetry, then a very long tail…

searchQuery.name: single-term-is-prefix-matched
searchQuery.why: results must narrow while the user is still typing the word

searchQuery.name: terms-are-conjoined-and-only-the-last-is-a-prefix
searchQuery.why: an earlier word the user finished typing is a whole word

searchQuery.name: case-is-folded
searchQuery.why: a search box is not case sensitive

searchQuery.name: fts-syntax-the-user-typed-is-data-not-syntax
searchQuery.why: an unbalanced quote is FTS5's problem, and must never become the user's

searchQuery.name: punctuation-alone-asks-nothing-of-the-index
searchQuery.why: null means `skip the content search`, not `error`

searchQuery.name: digits-are-terms
searchQuery.why: `100%` is a search for 100, and the percent sign is a separator

searchQuery.name: a-hyphen-separates
searchQuery.why: FTS tokenises on it too, so the rewrite must agree with the index

searchQuery.name: non-ascii-letters-are-alphanumeric
searchQuery.why: the split is on the Unicode Alphabetic/Number properties, not on [a-z0-9]

searchQuery.name: runs-of-separators-collapse
searchQuery.why: empty terms would produce `""` and an FTS error
